questions.stem: What is the very first thing you should do with any new SOHO router?
questions.explanation: Default logins are public knowledge, so the first step on any new router is to change the default administrator password.
questions.trap: Enabling UPnP and disabling the firewall both weaken security; the priority is changing the default credentials.

questions.stem: Why is keeping a router's firmware updated important?

choices.text: Firmware updates add new wallpaper themes
Firmware is the router's OS, and updates contain critical security patches
Firmware updates increase the Wi-Fi password length automatically

questions.explanation: Firmware is the router's operating system; updates contain critical security patches that fix known vulnerabilities.
questions.trap: Firmware updates are security-critical, not cosmetic.

questions.stem: Which SOHO router feature is a major security risk because it lets internal applications automatically open firewall ports, and should be disabled?
questions.explanation: UPnP lets internal applications automatically open ports on the firewall, which is a security nightmare. The review says to always disable it.
questions.trap: WPA3 and a guest network are good security practices; UPnP is the one to turn off.

questions.stem: A public-facing web server needs to be reachable from the internet while staying isolated from the private internal network. Where should it be placed?

choices.text: On the main LAN with the workstations

questions.explanation: A screened subnet (DMZ) is a secure reception area: internet visitors can reach the web server there, but they cannot get into the private internal network.
questions.trap: Putting the public server on the main LAN exposes the internal network if the server is compromised.

questions.stem: A technician disables SSID broadcast and considers the wireless network secured. What is the correct assessment?

choices.text: It is only security through obscurity and does not stop a determined attacker; strong encryption is what matters
It fully secures the network on its own
It is required before enabling WPA3

questions.explanation: Hiding the SSID is just security through obscurity; a determined attacker can still find the network. What really matters is strong encryption (WPA2/WPA3).
questions.trap: Disabling SSID broadcast does not encrypt anything and is not a substitute for WPA2/WPA3.

questions.stem: What is the minimum recommended wireless encryption for a SOHO network, with the ideal being one step higher?

choices.text: No encryption is needed on a guest network

questions.explanation: Use at a minimum WPA2 and ideally WPA3 for wireless encryption.
questions.trap: WEP is obsolete and insecure; it is never an acceptable minimum.

questions.stem: A home has many IoT gadgets and frequent visitors. Which configuration keeps them off the main trusted network while still giving internet access?
questions.explanation: A guest network gives visitors and less-secure IoT devices internet access while isolating them from the main trusted devices.
questions.trap: Port forwarding opens inbound holes; it does not isolate untrusted devices.

questions.stem: On a wired network, what is a critical best practice for physical switch ports in places like conference rooms?

choices.text: Leave all ports active for convenience
Forward all ports to the DMZ
Disable any unused physical network ports

questions.explanation: Disable unused physical network ports. An active open port in a conference room is an open invitation for an intruder to plug in.
questions.trap: Leaving every port live maximizes attack surface - the opposite of the best practice.

questions.stem: An admin must make an internal service reachable from the internet by mapping a public port to a specific internal IP and port. What is this, and what is the caution?

choices.text: Port forwarding; it creates a permanent 24/7 hole in the firewall, so use it only when necessary
UPnP; it is always safe to leave on
A DMZ; it requires no firewall rules
SSID hiding; it encrypts the service

questions.explanation: Port forwarding maps a public firewall port to an internal IP/port. The caution: it creates a permanent 24/7 hole in the firewall, so only use it when absolutely necessary.
questions.trap: UPnP automating port openings is exactly the risky behavior to avoid, not a safe alternative.

questions.stem: Routers can create deny lists to block specific malicious websites or entire categories of content. What is this capability called?
questions.explanation: Routers can perform IP and content filtering, letting you build deny lists that block malicious sites or whole content categories.
questions.trap: Port forwarding opens access inbound; it is not the mechanism for blocking outbound site categories.
